chains.title: Alt T creates a stronger FOXA1 (forkhead) site in a luminal enhancer, raising expression of a nearby 14q22.1 gene
chains.element: Putative distal enhancer at chr14:55,887,040 active in ER+ luminal breast epithelium (MCF7)

links.claim: The C>T change is predicted to improve match to the forkhead core motif (TGTTT/GTAAACA family), so the alt allele is bound more strongly by FOXA1; FOXA1 is chosen within the forkhead specificity group because it is the dominant, highly expressed forkhead factor in MCF7 and in luminal breast tissue (FOXA2/FOXA3 are essentially absent).
The variant lies in a non-coding region expected to carry luminal enhancer marks (H3K27ac, ATAC accessibility) co-bound by FOXA1 in MCF7.
Stronger FOXA1 pioneering increases accessibility and looping of this enhancer to a 14q22.1 promoter, most plausibly SAMD4A, raising its transcription.
The effect is restricted to FOXA1-expressing luminal breast cells, where the enhancer is open.
Altered dosage of the FOXA1-driven target gene modestly shifts proliferation/differentiation of luminal progenitors, contributing to ER+ breast cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP-seq signal in heterozygous breast cells favours the T allele
EMSA supershift with FOXA1 antibody shows stronger complex on the T probe
FOXA1 knockdown abolishes the allelic reporter difference
Reporter activity higher for T than C in MCF7, no difference in FOXA1-negative cells (e.g. MDA-MB-231)
falsified_if: No allelic imbalance in FOXA1 ChIP or no FOXA1 occupancy at the locus
Reporter shows no allelic difference, or the C allele is more active
QBiC-SELEX forkhead models show the ref allele is the stronger binder

chains.title: Ref C preserves a GATA3 site; alt T disrupts it, lowering enhancer output
chains.element: Same putative luminal enhancer at chr14:55,887,040

links.claim: The C allele can complete a WGATAA-like core that the T allele breaks, so GATA3 binds the ref allele more; within the GATA specificity group GATA3 is chosen because it is the only GATA factor highly expressed in MCF7 and luminal breast tissue.
GATA3 co-occupies FOXA1/ER enhancers in luminal cells, and this site is expected to fall in such a cluster.
Loss of GATA3 binding on the risk allele reduces enhancer activity and lowers expression of the looped 14q22.1 target.
Restricted to GATA3-high luminal cells; no effect in basal/mesenchymal lines.
Reduced target-gene expression weakens luminal differentiation control, increasing ER+ breast cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP favours the C allele
GATA3 knockdown removes the allelic reporter difference while FOXA1 knockdown does not
Reporter activity lower for T than C
falsified_if: No GATA3 occupancy or no allelic imbalance at the site
T allele shows equal or higher reporter activity
Motif analysis shows no GATA core is created or destroyed

chains.title: Alt T weakens an ESR1 half-site/ERE, blunting oestrogen-responsive enhancer activity

links.claim: The variant sits in or beside an ERE half-site (GGTCA-like) that the C allele matches better, so ESR1 binds the ref allele more; ESR1 rather than ESR2 because ESR2 is not meaningfully expressed in MCF7.
The element is expected to be an E2-inducible ER binding site in MCF7.
Weaker ER recruitment on the alt allele reduces E2-induced transcription of the nearby target gene.
Effect confined to ER+ cells and dependent on oestrogen stimulation.
Altered oestrogen-responsive gene dosage shifts hormone-driven proliferation and ER+ breast cancer risk.

predictions: Allelic reporter difference appears only after E2 treatment and is lost with fulvestrant
ER ChIP shows E2-dependent occupancy with C-allele bias
No allelic effect in ER-negative cells even if FOXA1 is present
falsified_if: No ER binding at the locus in E2-treated MCF7
Allelic reporter difference is identical with and without oestrogen

chains.title: Alt T disrupts a CTCF site, altering TAD/loop insulation at 14q22.1
chains.target_gene: SAMD4A / GCH1 (enhancer-promoter rewiring within the sub-TAD)
chains.cell_type: Broadly expressed; phenotype read out in breast epithelium

links.claim: The C>T change falls in the core CTCF 19-mer and weakens binding, so the ref allele binds CTCF more; CTCF is a single-member specificity (CTCFL is testis-restricted and not expressed in MCF7).
The element acts as a constitutive loop anchor rather than a cell-type-specific enhancer.
Weaker insulation on the alt allele lets an adjacent enhancer contact a different promoter, changing expression of a 14q22.1 gene.
CTCF binding is ubiquitous, but the expression consequence is seen where the neighbouring enhancers are active, i.e. breast epithelium.
Rewired enhancer-promoter contacts alter target dosage and contribute to breast cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP/CUT&RUN favours C across many cell types, not just breast
Episomal reporter shows little or no allelic difference (insulators act in chromatin context)
falsified_if: No CTCF peak at the variant in any ENCODE cell type
Allelic effect is breast-restricted and reporter-detectable

next_experiment: Mine existing MCF7/breast ChIP-seq (FOXA1, GATA3, ER, CTCF) for allele-specific read imbalance at chr14:55,887,040 in heterozygous samples, together with a QBiC-SELEX lookup of these TFs. This costs nothing new and immediately separates the null (no peak or balanced reads) from the FOXA1 chain (T-biased FOXA1 occupancy).
